items.note: The page proves the isomorphism, derives the triangular formula, explains the descending update order after reordering the axes to (a_1,...,a_d), and totals the cost from O(d^2) chunk-interchange moves to O(Tp d^2(1+ell^tau)), as the paper does (lines 4204-4292).
Defines P_i as the prefix product and mu_i = P_i^{-1} mod s_i, and justifies that the inverse exists: "It is invertible because P_i is coprime to s_i", which follows from pairwise coprimality.
"Since s_i | S, each x_i^{mu_i S}=1, so Phi respects x^S=1 and defines an algebra map" correctly spells out the check that the paper only asserts.

Shows Phi(x^k)=1 iff s_i | mu_i k for all i, iff s_i | k (mu_i a unit), iff S | k (pairwise coprime). So x has image of order S, its S powers are distinct and fill the S target monomials, and Phi is an isomorphism preserving convolution. This follows the paper's reasoning, in more detail.

Writes k = sum a_j P_j with 0 <= a_j < s_j, notes that b_i = mu_i k mod s_i, and reaches the paper's formula b_i = a_i + mu_i sum_{j<i} a_j P_j (mod s_i). The worked example with s=(3,5) and k=4, giving (1,3), checks out.
"Terms with j>i vanish modulo s_i, since s_i divides P_j, and mu_i P_i = 1 modulo s_i" is exactly the paper's justification, with the reason for divisibility stated.

Reorders the axes to (a_1,...,a_d) and updates i=d,...,1 so that the lower-index controls still hold the original digits. Each update is a cyclic shift of [0,s_i) with the identity on [s_i,t_i), so padding stays zero, as in the paper. The paper's explicit identity rule for an invalid lower-index control (line 4263) is not mentioned, but the conclusion does not need it.

Axes have ell or ell-1 bits. An unequal pair is swapped by moving the leading bit out, swapping the equal-width pair with an O(V L^tau) chunk interchange, and putting the bit back. Reversal takes O(d^2) moves, and shifts and scans cost O(dTp). Together these give O(Tp d^2(1+ell^tau)), matching the paper.

errors.quote: The map is implemented by these shifts, each of linear cost by [Controlled shifts and rational scalings](controlled-shifts.md), which includes computing the offsets.
errors.problem: The paper gives the controlled-shift cost as O(V) apart from computing the offsets (line 1956); the lemma covers offsets only for a fixed number of controls, whereas target i here has i-1 controls. The paper bounds the offsets separately (lines 4279-4281): there are at most T/t_i control prefixes, so all offsets cost O(dTp^C/r)=o(Tp), because t_i >= r/2 and r exceeds every fixed power of p. The page credits this to the lemma instead. The linear total is still correct.
